title: Choose an ArangoDB access path from the query shape
description: Select a real application question, then compare key-value, document, and graph modeling. The result changes the lookup path, required index, and maintenance cost without inventing benchmark numbers.

models.label: Key-value access
models.detail: Use the document key and built-in primary index when the caller already knows the identity.

models.label: Document query
models.detail: Filter, sort, project, or aggregate JSON attributes with AQL and deliberate secondary indexes.

models.label: Graph traversal
models.detail: Store nodes and directed edge documents when paths or neighborhoods are the central result.

queryShapes.label: Load one profile by ID
queryShapes.prompt: The API receives user key u-184 and must return that user's current profile document.
requestShape: The caller already knows the immutable document key.
The result is one document, not an attribute search or relationship path.
No secondary ordering or traversal is required.

key-value.headline: Use the primary-key path directly
key-value.explanation: ArangoDB's key-value model is a subset of its document model. Every collection has a primary index on _key, so the known identity is already the access path.
key-value.indexPlan: Use the built-in primary index on _key or _id. Do not add a duplicate secondary index for the same identity.
key-value.tradeoff: The path cannot answer arbitrary attribute predicates. A later search by email, city, or status needs a separate indexed document query.

document.headline: A document query works, but it adds no value here
document.explanation: AQL can filter by _key and the optimizer can use the primary index, but the request already has the exact identity. Keep the query simple and avoid disguising a point lookup as a broad scan.
path: Enter an AQL FOR and FILTER
document.indexPlan: Filter by _key equality so the primary index remains usable. Verify the plan instead of assuming every FILTER becomes a point lookup.
document.tradeoff: The additional query structure is justified only if the request also needs projections, joins, aggregation, or another AQL operation.

graph.headline: A vertex is still a document, but no edge is needed
graph.explanation: Graph nodes are documents and can be loaded by key. Creating or traversing edges for a request that only needs one profile would add relationship state without answering a relationship question.
graph.indexPlan: Use the vertex collection's primary index. The automatic edge indexes on _from and _to do not help this point lookup.
graph.tradeoff: Model the profile as a graph node only when other important queries traverse its relationships; the point read alone does not justify graph maintenance.

queryShapes.label: Filter and sort a catalog
queryShapes.prompt: A listing page needs active laptops in one category, ordered by rating, with only six projected fields.
requestShape: The caller does not know document keys in advance.
The query combines equality filters, ordering, projection, and a limit.
Relationships between products are not part of the result.

key-value.headline: Known-key retrieval cannot express the catalog predicate
key-value.explanation: A primary-key map answers which document owns a known key. It does not discover every active laptop or order those documents by rating.
path: Scan records or maintain a second mapping
Sort and limit outside the key lookup
key-value.indexPlan: A separate secondary access path is required. Once that path supports category, status, and rating, this is a document query rather than pure key-value access.
key-value.tradeoff: Maintaining ad hoc lookup maps duplicates index work and creates another consistency boundary between the map and the product documents.

document.headline: Shape one indexed AQL document query
document.explanation: The result is selected from document attributes, so use AQL with a persistent index designed from the equality filters and requested ordering.
document.indexPlan: Test a persistent index whose leading fields match the equality predicates and whose remaining order supports the sort. Confirm with EXPLAIN and representative data.
document.tradeoff: Every useful secondary index adds storage and write maintenance. An index should earn that cost through an observed query shape.

graph.headline: Vertex documents can be filtered, but traversal is unnecessary
graph.explanation: Graph vertices remain regular documents, so AQL can filter them. The graph model adds value only when product relationships enter the question.
path: Run the same attribute index path
graph.indexPlan: Use a persistent index on the vertex collection's queried attributes. Edge indexes do not accelerate a product-only filter.
graph.tradeoff: If recommendations or compatibility edges are not part of this request, graph definitions and edge lifecycles are extra operational state.

queryShapes.label: Trace a two-hop fraud neighborhood
queryShapes.prompt: An investigator starts from one account and asks which other accounts share a device or payment instrument within two directed hops.
requestShape: The answer is a path through changing many-to-many relationships.
Direction and traversal depth are part of the query contract.
The result needs both connected entities and relationship evidence.

key-value.headline: Point lookups cannot discover an unknown neighborhood
key-value.explanation: The first account key is known, but the connected device, instrument, and account keys are the result of the query. A key-value path cannot discover them without a separately maintained adjacency structure.
path: Deduplicate paths and fetch every result
key-value.indexPlan: Application-owned adjacency documents become a graph index in disguise. Their update, cleanup, and dangling-reference rules must be made explicit.
key-value.tradeoff: Every relationship change can touch several adjacency copies. Partial retries can leave one side of the relationship stale.

document.headline: Embedded references work only for bounded, stable neighborhoods
document.explanation: Documents can embed related IDs and AQL can join collections, but a many-to-many network with frequent changes creates fan-out, duplicate references, and manual path logic.
document.indexPlan: Index every join key used by the hop expansion. Measure the actual fan-out and bound depth so one request cannot grow without limit.
document.tradeoff: Embedding favors reads but makes relationship updates and delete cleanup harder. Normalized references reduce duplication but turn traversal into repeated joins.

graph.headline: Represent the evidence as edge documents
graph.explanation: ArangoDB edge documents carry _from and _to references plus relationship properties. AQL can traverse a bounded neighborhood and return vertices, edges, and paths together.
graph.indexPlan: Use the automatic edge indexes on _from and _to, then add vertex-centric indexes only for selective edge filters that the measured traversal needs.
graph.tradeoff: Traversal depth and branching must stay bounded. Low-selectivity edges can expand the neighborhood rapidly even though the syntax is concise.

queryShapes.label: Combine a profile filter with relationship evidence
queryShapes.prompt: A risk review starts from active business accounts, traverses ownership edges, and returns owners whose profile documents match a jurisdiction rule.
requestShape: Document attributes select the starting accounts and final owners.
Ownership edges connect entities that live in separate collections.
One query must preserve the relationship path as evidence.

key-value.headline: The request does not begin with every required key
key-value.explanation: Several keys are discovered by filtering and traversal. Pure key-value access would need external indexes plus application-side graph assembly.
key-value.indexPlan: Each external mapping needs its own consistency and recovery contract. The primary index alone cannot select accounts by status or owners by jurisdiction.
key-value.tradeoff: The application becomes the query engine and must reconcile partial reads across several independently maintained mappings.

document.headline: AQL joins can express the query with explicit references
document.explanation: Document collections and indexed foreign-reference fields can join accounts to ownership records and owners. This can fit when the relationship depth is fixed and small.
document.indexPlan: Index account status, both ownership reference fields, and the owner jurisdiction predicate. Confirm that the fixed joins stay selective.
document.tradeoff: As path depth or relationship types grow, nested joins become harder to reason about and every new hop needs another explicit access path.

graph.headline: Compose document filters and graph traversal in one AQL query
graph.explanation: The native multi-model value is visible here: AQL can filter starting documents, traverse ownership edges, inspect owner attributes, and return the path without synchronizing a separate graph store.
path: Filter owners and return path evidence
graph.indexPlan: Use persistent indexes for the document predicates and automatic edge indexes for traversal. In a cluster, shard placement must also match the dominant path.
graph.tradeoff: One query language does not remove distributed-query cost. Cross-shard traversals and broad starting sets can still create network fan-out.
